skill.grandcraft.warrior.root.descriptio: Blocking well opens the way in. Absorb a blow without your guard breaking and you move quicker for five seconds, and your next blow lands far harder — including against a raised guard, which it drains all the faster. Connecting spends it, so pick the swing.
skill.grandcraft.outlaw.root.description: The Outlaw is a keen acrobat — able to jump again in mid-air and throw themself onward, to catch a wall two blocks tall and hang from it, and to kick off it wherever they are looking. Two walls before the ground is owed a moment; hanging drains stamina and blunts the swing.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.skill_root.toolt: Your class's own passive, in force from the moment you chose it. Never locked, and it costs you nothing to keep. All three lines begin here.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.skill_node.toolt: No ability is bound to this node yet. The abilities are still to be designed; this is the shape they will hang on.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.equip.locked: That skill is not unlocked yet.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.equip.full: All three ability slots are full — take one off first.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.skill_fired: Ability %s — nothing bound to it yet
screen.grandcraft.sheet.objective.slay_w: Slay %s hostiles with a class skill
screen.grandcraft.sheet.strength.tooltip: The force behind everything you swing. Every weapon converts some mixture of stats into damage, and heavy ones convert Strength almost exclusively — a claymore reads nothing else. It also decides which weapons you can lift at all: fall short of what one requires and it deals 1 damage no matter how good it is.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.agility.tooltip: The force behind light and fast weapons — a dagger reads mostly Agility, a sword partly. Already in force: every stamina cost — attacking, dodging, jumping, sprinting, guarding — is %s%% of normal.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.constitution.too: How much punishment you can take. Already in force: %s armour, %s maximum health, and stamina recovers at %s%% of normal.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.arcane.tooltip: The force behind your spells, and behind the implements that cast them — a staff scales off Arcane in melee as well. Every point above 10 makes what you cast hit harder, and every point below makes it weaker. It does not yet touch the size of your mana pool or how fast it returns.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.health.tooltip: What you can lose before you die. Constitution raises the ceiling but does not fill it — gaining it never heals you.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.stamina.tooltip: Spent on every committed action. Empty it and you are locked out until it recovers, which is the mistake the whole system is built around.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.mana.tooltip: What your spells are paid for out of. It only recovers on its own once your Arcane is high enough — below that you can still cast, but you have to find mana rather than wait for it.
class.grandcraft.warrior.description: Meets the attack head on. Armour, endurance, and the stamina to hold a guard long after anyone else has dropped theirs.
class.grandcraft.outlaw.description: Never where the blow lands. Light and quick, and everything you commit to — every dodge, every swing — costs you less.
class.grandcraft.sorcerer.description: Fragile within reach, and never intends to be there. Trades armour and muscle for raw arcane force.
class.grandcraft.cleric.description: Holds the line for someone else. Hard to put down, and carries power that mends as readily as it breaks.
weapon.grandcraft.category.medium.descri: All medium weapons — swords and axes.
weapon.grandcraft.category.heavy.descrip: All heavy weapons — claymores and maces.
weapon.grandcraft.category.arcane.descri: All casting implements — staves. Cannot guard.
weapon.grandcraft.category.ranged.descri: All ranged weapons — bows and crossbows.
weapon.grandcraft.category.unarmed.descr: Bare hands, and any tool that is not a weapon.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.title: Weapon Settings
screen.grandcraft.weapons.subtitle: Each value applies to every weapon in the category.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.wind_up_modifi: Ticks added to your wind-up when holding this kind of weapon, on top of the Wind-up on the Player tab of the combat settings. It can be negative: -2 makes this weapon quicker to telegraph than the rest, +5 slower. Zero means the weapon keeps the same rhythm as everything else, which is what most of them should do — the telegraph is only readable because it is mostly one length.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.hit_window.too: How long the swing can connect for, once the wind-up finishes. A longer wind-up needs a longer window or the swing cannot land on anything that is moving: a target walking backwards covers ground during the telegraph, so a slow weapon with a short window defeats itself.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.endlag_modifie: Ticks added to your endlag when holding this kind of weapon, on top of the Endlag on the Player tab of the combat settings. Negative values are allowed. This is the strongest lever a weapon has: endlag is the whole cost of a miss, and the zombie attack cycle is 17 ticks, so +10 here means a zombie that starts winding up as you swing lands its hit before you can answer.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.stamina_cost.t: What one swing takes out of the pool. Divide the pool by this for the number of swings from full — and remember the regen delay restarts on every spend, so a weapon swung continuously recovers nothing at all.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.mana_cost.tool: What one cast takes out of the mana pool. Set the mana pool itself to 0 in the stat settings to turn casting off entirely.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.base_damage.to: Damage before the Arcane multiplier, in hundredths: 200 is 2 damage. This is the attack a caster has when they have nothing better, so it is meant to be modest — that is what makes real spells worth learning.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.projectile_spe: How fast the gust flies, in hundredths of a block per tick: 150 is 1.5 blocks a tick, or 30 blocks a second.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.knockback.tool: How hard a hit shoves its target along the direction of flight, in hundredths of a block per tick. A plain vanilla hit is about 40. Zero by default: a gust that pushed made distance too cheap to create. Left available for a heavier spell that should.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.cooldown.toolt: How long the implement is unusable after a cast, before Arcane is taken into account — a high-Arcane caster waits less. The final figure never drops below 5 ticks whatever you set here, because a held right-click repeats every 4 and anything shorter stops gating anything at all.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.range.tooltip: How many ticks the projectile flies before it gives up. The gust has no gravity, so one that hits nothing would otherwise never despawn — do not set this to 0.
screen.grandcraft.stats.title: Stat Tuning
screen.grandcraft.stats.armour_per_const: Armour points gained per point of Constitution above 10, in hundredths — 50 means half a point each. Below 10 it costs armour instead. Minecraft caps total armour at 30 including worn gear, so a large value here is quietly clipped rather than refused.
screen.grandcraft.stats.health_per_const: Maximum health gained per point of Constitution above 10, in hundredths of a half-heart. Deliberately slight: Constitution is meant to make you harder to kill, not to make every fight longer. Raising it does not heal you — it raises the ceiling and leaves you to fill it.
screen.grandcraft.stats.stamina_regen_pe: Percent faster stamina recovery per point of Constitution above 10. This is how long you can keep making choices in a fight, so it is felt across a whole encounter rather than on any one action.
screen.grandcraft.stats.stamina_cost_per: Percent cheaper every stamina cost becomes per point of Agility above 10 — attacks, dodges, jumps, sprinting and blocking alike. The total is clamped so no amount of Agility can make an action free.
screen.grandcraft.stats.max_mana.tooltip: The size of the mana pool. Nothing spends mana yet; this exists so the magic layer arrives to a resource that already works. Zero switches mana off entirely.
screen.grandcraft.stats.mana_regen_per_s: Mana recovered per second, for a character whose Arcane clears the threshold below. Deliberately slow: this is meant to be the floor that potions, enchantments, gear and passive abilities build on, not the whole supply.
screen.grandcraft.stats.mana_regen_min_a: The Arcane a character needs before mana recovers on its own at all. Below it a staff still casts, but only from mana already banked. This is what stops every class carrying a staff for a free projectile: at 15 only a Sorcerer starts above it, and a Cleric reaches it after two stat points. Set to 0 to give everyone recovery.
screen.grandcraft.stats.mana_regen_delay: Ticks of pause after spending mana before it starts coming back. Twenty ticks is one second. Has no effect until something can spend mana.
screen.grandcraft.game.title: GrandCraft Settings
screen.grandcraft.game.health_bars.toolt: Show a health bar above an entity for two seconds after it takes damage. Applies to every player on the server, and replaces that entity's name tag while it is up.
screen.grandcraft.game.combat_animations: Show attack wind-up, commitment and recovery as poses, so a swing can be read before it lands. Turning this off leaves the timings untouched — the attacks still happen, they just become invisible.
screen.grandcraft.config.title: Combat Tuning
screen.grandcraft.config.dodge_invulnera: How long a dodge makes attacks miss, starting on the very first tick. Long enough and a dodge always beats an attack already in flight; short enough and only a well-timed one does.
How long after the invulnerability ends before the roll can act again. This is the entire cost of dodging: dodge at the wrong moment and the next attack lands while you are still stuck in this.
screen.grandcraft.config.dodge_speed.too: How hard the roll launches, in hundredths of a block per tick. Physics decays it, so this sets how far the roll carries rather than a fixed distance. Very high values outrun collision and put actors through corners.
screen.grandcraft.config.dodge_cost.tool: What one dodge takes out of the pool. Set above an attack's cost so trading swings for dodges is a real decision rather than a free extra option.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_raise.too: How long the guard takes to come up, during which it stops nothing at all. This is the whole cost of blocking, paid in advance — the mirror of a dodge, which protects at once and charges afterwards. Long enough and only reading the wind-up early gets the guard up in time.
How long after letting go before the actor can act again. Stops the guard being flicked up and down for free, so dropping it to attack is a decision rather than a reflex.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_break.too: How long the stagger lasts when the pool runs dry behind a raised guard. The hit that empties it is still blocked; this is the punishment that follows. Always applied, unlike an ordinary stagger, because a guard break is a mistake made with your own resource.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_cost.tool: Stamina spent per point of damage absorbed, in hundredths — 250 means two and a half. Tune this against a whole fight, not one swing: blocking is continuous under pressure, so a cost that looks fair per hit can empty the pool in seconds.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_hold.tool: Stamina spent per second simply holding the guard up. Doing more than it looks: spending anything at all is what stops the pool regenerating behind a raised guard, so setting this to zero lets an actor recover while still blocking.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_arc.toolt: How far to either side of where the actor faces the guard reaches, so 180 covers everything and 90 covers only what is in front of the shoulders. Below about 120 the edge sits where a crowding attacker stands, and the same attack starts blocking or landing at random.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_slow.tool: How much movement speed is given up while the guard is up. The trade the verb is built on — safety for mobility — and what stops blocking being something to walk around behind.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_shield.to: What a shield multiplies the absorb cost by, against blocking bare-handed with a weapon. Below 100 a shield blocks more cheaply, which is the whole reason to carry one now that vanilla's own blocking is gone.
screen.grandcraft.config.startup.tooltip: Wind-up ticks before the blow lands — the telegraph, and the window in which the swing is already committed. For a mob it is the window in which hitting it first cancels its attack, and in which you can step out of range to make it whiff; long values make a mob easy to shut down, so pair a long wind-up with a wider Hit Window or the attack can never land. On the Player tab this is the global: one wind-up for every weapon, so a swing teaches one rhythm.
screen.grandcraft.config.active.tooltip: Ticks during which the blow can actually connect. The mob commits at the start of its wind-up, so by the time this opens the target may have walked out of a reach of about 1.4 blocks — a long wind-up therefore needs a wide window, or the mob telegraphs, commits and whiffs every time. One hit only, however wide it is set.
screen.grandcraft.config.recovery.toolti: Ticks this actor is locked after swinging, before it can attack again. Nothing to do with regenerating health. Together with startup this is the whole attack cycle — nothing else paces it, and it is the entire cost of a whiff. On the Player tab this is the global: one endlag for every weapon.
screen.grandcraft.config.stagger.tooltip: How long a hit staggers this actor: slowed and unable to attack. A second hit soon after gives half of this, and a third gives nothing, which is what stops a fast weapon locking a mob down forever.
screen.grandcraft.config.health.tooltip: Base stats: the starting point that later features add to rather than replace. Health, damage and speed are typed as whole percent of this actor's vanilla value, so 100 is unchanged and 150 is half again. A mob rolls its base once between min and max when it first spawns and keeps that roll for life — set min and max apart to get a spread of difficulties. Health and damage go to 2000, speed to 1000, though much past 300 speed the pathfinding stops keeping up.
screen.grandcraft.config.defence.tooltip: Armour points, not a multiplier — vanilla mobs have none, so there is nothing to multiply. Each point cuts incoming damage roughly 4%, to a maximum of 30.
screen.grandcraft.config.max_stamina.too: The size of this actor’s stamina pool. Every action is priced against it, so raising this makes an actor able to do more before it has to stop rather than making any single action cheaper. Set to 0 to turn stamina off for this actor entirely.
screen.grandcraft.config.regen.tooltip: Stamina refilled per second, once the delay below has passed. Nothing regenerates while stamina is being spent, so a sprint cost is really “how many seconds of sprinting the pool holds” and this is only how fast it comes back afterwards.
screen.grandcraft.config.regen_delay.too: Ticks after any spend before stamina starts coming back. Refreshed by every spend, so a continuous cost such as sprinting holds regeneration off for as long as it runs. Emptying the pool adds a further 20 ticks on top of this.
screen.grandcraft.config.attack_cost.too: Stamina spent per swing, charged whether it hit or missed. This is what makes a whiff a real mistake and what stops attacking being spammable. An actor with too little stamina to pay simply cannot attack.
screen.grandcraft.config.sprint_cost.too: Stamina drained per second of sprinting. Since nothing regenerates while it is being spent, pool divided by this is roughly how many seconds of continuous sprint the actor has. Sprinting stops the moment the pool empties. Set to 0 to leave sprinting free.
screen.grandcraft.config.jump_cost.toolt: Stamina spent per jump. Mobs are prevented from jumping when they cannot pay; the player is stopped by their own client, since a jump has already happened by the time the server hears about it. Set to 0 to leave jumping free.
screen.grandcraft.config.reset.tooltip: Restores the values on the open tab to their shipped defaults. Other tabs are left alone, and nothing is applied until you press Save.
commands.grandcraft.reclass.success: %s has been reset to Peasant and may choose a new class
commands.grandcraft.set_essence.success: %s is now Essence Power level %s, with %s stat points and %s attribute points to spend. Anything previously spent was cleared.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.spend.tooltip: Spend one point on %s. Permanent — points cannot be moved once committed.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.pool_points.tool: Attribute points earned at milestone levels, waiting to be spent on the Health, Stamina or Mana pools. Use the buttons on the rows below. Buying a pool raises its ceiling and leaves you to fill it — it is not a heal.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.level.tooltip: Your Essence Power level. It rises by collecting Life Essence Orbs, which every mob drops when you kill it. Each level grants a stat point, and every fifth level also grants attribute points. Vanilla experience levels are a separate thing entirely and are not shown here.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.essence.tooltip: Essence collected towards your next level, against what that level costs. The difference between the two is how much more you need. Each level costs more than the one before it.
screen.grandcraft.stats.health_per_pool_: Maximum health gained per attribute point spent on Health, in half-hearts — 2 is one heart per point. Whole numbers here, unlike the per-Constitution figure above, because an attribute point is a rare deliberate purchase rather than a slight passive effect. Raising the ceiling does not heal you.
screen.grandcraft.stats.stamina_per_pool: Maximum stamina gained per attribute point spent on Stamina. At the default attack cost of 12, ten points here is most of an extra swing per purchase. The pool does not refill on purchase — the new room has to be earned back.
screen.grandcraft.stats.mana_per_pool_po: Maximum mana gained per attribute point spent on Mana. Has no effect at all while the mana pool above is set to zero.
screen.grandcraft.stats.spell_damage_per: How much each point of Arcane above 10 adds to spell damage, and each point below takes away. At 5%% a Sorcerer starting at 16 casts for 30%% more than neutral and a Warrior at 6 for 20%% less. The finished multiplier is clamped between 25%% and 300%%, so an extreme value here is strong rather than absurd.
screen.grandcraft.stats.spell_cooldown_p: How much each point of Arcane above 10 shortens the wait between casts, and each point below lengthens it. This compounds with spell damage, so investing in Arcane buys both force and rate. No amount of Arcane can take a cooldown below 5 ticks — under that a held right-click simply repeats and the cooldown stops meaning anything.
screen.grandcraft.skills.title: Skill Tuning
screen.grandcraft.skills.combat_master_d: Extra damage on the empowered blow, in whole percent — 50 means half again. It also reaches a defender's guard, since blocking costs stamina in proportion to the damage absorbed, so raising this makes the Warrior better at breaking a turtle open as well as at killing. Set to 0 to leave the blow ordinary.
screen.grandcraft.skills.combat_master_s: Movement bonus while the window is open, in whole percent. Composes with the guard's own slowdown rather than replacing it, so a Warrior who blocks again mid-window is both slowed and quickened. Set to 0 for no movement change.
screen.grandcraft.skills.combat_master_w: How long the window lasts after a clean block, in ticks — 20 to the second. Blocking again restarts it rather than extending it, so it cannot be banked. Set to 0 to switch Combat Master off entirely.
screen.grandcraft.skills.acrobat_dash_sp: How hard the dash throws you sideways, in hundredths of a block per tick. Air drag makes the distance roughly 7.5 times this, so 60 covers about four and a half blocks — half again a sprint-jump. Do not copy the dodge's 95 in here: a dodge only travels two blocks because it happens on the ground against friction, and the same figure in the air is over seven. Set to 0 to switch Acrobat off entirely, wall grips included.
screen.grandcraft.skills.acrobat_dash_li: How hard the dash throws you upward, in hundredths of a block per tick. 25 peaks at about half a block. This replaces your vertical motion rather than adding to it, which is what lets a dash cancel a fall — and also means dashing while still rising from a jump cuts the climb short rather than doubling it. Set to 0 for a flat dash with no hop.
screen.grandcraft.skills.acrobat_dash_co: Stamina each dash costs, before Agility. Three dashes at 12 is a third of a default pool, and a full two-wall traversal — jump, three dashes and two short hangs — runs about 80 of 100. Set to 0 to make dashing free.
screen.grandcraft.skills.acrobat_wall_ho: How many walls can be caught before you have to settle on the ground again. This is the only thing bounding the chain: catching a wall hands the dash back, so without a limit here an Outlaw who kept finding walls could fly. Set to 0 to leave the dash on its own with no wall grips at all.
screen.grandcraft.skills.acrobat_hang_dr: Stamina a second while hanging on a wall, before Agility. Note that draining also holds the regen delay open, so nothing recovers at all while you hang — a grip is a fixed budget rather than a rate contest, which is what stops a wall being somewhere to rest out of reach of the mobs below. Set to 0 to make hanging free, which also restores regen behind it.
screen.grandcraft.skills.acrobat_hang_da: How much weaker your swings are while hanging, in whole percent off. It reaches a defender's guard too, since blocking costs stamina in proportion to the damage absorbed, so an Outlaw on a wall is worse at breaking a guard as well as at killing. Set to 0 to fight from a wall at full strength.
screen.grandcraft.skills.acrobat_hit_cos: Stamina lost when a hit knocks you off a wall, on top of losing the grip. Charged whether or not you can afford it. A hit your guard absorbed does not count — blocking on a wall keeps you there. Set to 0 to be knocked off for free.
screen.grandcraft.skills.acrobat_ground_: How long you must stand on the ground, in ticks, before your wall grips come back — and it has to be unbroken, so brief touches never add up. The dash itself is not gated by this and returns the instant you land, so a player who lands and jumps straight away always has their move. Set to 0 to have any touch of the ground restore the grips.
screen.grandcraft.skills.acrobat_hook_co: How long after letting go of a wall, in ticks, before another can be caught. Without it, dashing along a wall while looking parallel to it regrips on the very next tick and burns every grip in a moment — which reads as the second wall grip simply not working. 4 ticks is about two blocks of travel; much more than that and a narrow alley stops being wall-jumpable. Set to 0 to allow an immediate regrip.
screen.grandcraft.essence.level_up.point: %s stat point and %s attribute points to spend
screen.grandcraft.levels.title: Essence Power Tuning
screen.grandcraft.levels.base_cost.toolt: Essence needed for the very first level. At the default drop weights a kill is worth about 1.18 Essence, so 10 here is roughly nine kills. Cannot be zero: a level that costs nothing would be granted forever.
Extra Essence each level costs over the one before it. At 5, level 1 costs the base amount, level 5 costs four increases more, and so on. Set to 0 for a flat curve where every level costs the same.
screen.grandcraft.levels.drop_weight_1.t: How often a kill drops an orb worth 1 Essence, relative to the other two weights. These are shares rather than percentages, so 85/12/3 and 850/120/30 mean the same thing.
screen.grandcraft.levels.drop_weight_2.t: How often a kill drops an orb worth 2 Essence, relative to the other two weights. A larger orb is drawn larger, so raising this is visible as well as felt.
screen.grandcraft.levels.drop_weight_3.t: How often a kill drops an orb worth 3 Essence, relative to the other two weights. Kept rare by default so a big orb reads as a piece of luck.
screen.grandcraft.levels.stat_points_per: Points granted every level, spent on Strength, Agility, Constitution or Arcane. These are Stats, not the Health, Stamina and Mana pools — those are Attributes and are granted at milestones instead.
screen.grandcraft.levels.milestone_inter: How many levels apart the milestone levels are. A milestone grants attribute points on top of that level’s usual stat point. Cannot be zero.
screen.grandcraft.levels.pool_points_per: Points granted at each milestone level, spent on the Health, Stamina and Mana pools. These are Attributes, and are deliberately rarer than the stat points every level gives.
screen.grandcraft.levels.skill_tier_1_le: The Essence Power level at which the first row of every skill-line becomes reachable. A node still needs its own milestone completed on top of this. Set to 0 to open the row immediately.
screen.grandcraft.levels.skill_tier_2_le: As above, for the second row. Judge this against the cost curve at the top of this screen rather than on its own — at the default costs, level 25 is roughly 1,500 kills away.
screen.grandcraft.levels.skill_tier_3_le: As above, for the third row. At the default costs this is roughly 5,600 kills.
screen.grandcraft.levels.skill_tier_4_le: As above, for the deepest row. At the default costs this is roughly 12,400 kills — if that is not what you intended, the cost fields at the top of this screen are the lever, not this one.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.rules.descript: Values shared by every weapon, whatever kind it is.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.weight_strengt: How much this kind of weapon reads Strength when working out its damage. Shares are relative to each other, not to 100 — 60 and 40 mean the same thing as 30 and 20 — but keeping the four at a total of 100 is what lets you read each one as a percentage. A weapon also demands a minimum of whichever stat has the largest share here, so raising one changes what the whole category requires.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.weight_agility: How much this kind of weapon reads Agility. This is what makes a dagger an Outlaw’s weapon and a claymore a Warrior’s: the shares decide which character a weapon rewards, more than any damage figure does.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.weight_constit: How much this kind of weapon reads Constitution. Ships at zero everywhere, and is here so a weapon that genuinely rewards toughness has somewhere to say so. Raising it to make a category stronger is a damage lever wearing a design decision’s clothes — the Rules page is the honest place for that.
How much this kind of weapon reads Arcane. Set high on arcane implements so a staff is worth swinging for a caster and worth nothing for anyone else.
screen.grandcraft.weapons.weapon_base.to: How much of a weapon’s own damage survives, as a percentage, before stats multiply it. This is the single lever that decides how much of a fight is the weapon and how much is the character. At 50 a diamond sword contributes 4 of its 7 and the rest comes from you; turn it up and gear matters more, turn it down and levels do. Your bare hands are never reduced — that 1 damage is yours, not a weapon’s.
What a swing deals when the holder does not meet the weapon’s stat requirement, in hundredths — 100 is 1 damage. Deliberately not zero: a hit that deals nothing sets no invulnerability frames and plays no hurt sound, so it reads as a broken mod rather than as a weapon you cannot lift.
screen.grandcraft.stats.melee_damage_per: Percent more melee damage per point of a weapon’s scaling stat above what that weapon requires. The one rate here measured against a requirement rather than against 10, because a weapon states its own demand and meeting it exactly is what counts as normal. At 10%% a character twenty points past a claymore’s requirement hits three times as hard as one who has just qualified — this is the number that makes a class visible in a fight and a level worth reaching. The finished multiplier is clamped between 50%% and 500%%.
